package_info.why_malicious: These versions were published via a compromised maintainer account and contain injected code that hijacks user wallet transactions, redirecting funds to an attacker-controlled wallet. The malicious code abuses the trust in the official package distribution channel, resulting in direct financial theft from users.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user initiates wallet connection or transaction via dApp)
execution_context.file_location: dist/index.js (minified main bundle of Ledger Connect Kit)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: MinimaDrainerValue='0x1.main0drainValue', ... // code that hooks into wallet connection and transaction signing flows, rerouting transaction data to attacker wallet
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code intercepts wallet connection and transaction signing events, modifies the transaction destination address to an attacker-controlled wallet, and submits the altered transaction, resulting in user funds being drained.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and modifying transaction data to redirect funds is a classic sign of a drainer malware. The code is obfuscated/minified and not present in legitimate versions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal wallet connectors only facilitate user-approved transactions without altering transaction data or redirecting funds. This code actively manipulates user intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wallet connectors may prompt users for transaction approval, but never silently alter transaction destinations.
key_indicators: Presence of 'MinimaDrainerValue' and similar obfuscated variables
Hooks into wallet connection and transaction signing flows
Silent modification of transaction destination addresses
No corresponding source code or release tags in official Git repository

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when dApp loads wallet connection modal)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: // Malicious modal overlay: injects a rogue WalletConnect option that routes through attacker infrastructure
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects a malicious 'Connect Wallet' modal overlay, presenting a rogue WalletConnect option that, when selected, routes wallet connections through attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting a fake or rogue wallet connection option is a common phishing tactic to capture or manipulate user wallet interactions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate wallet connectors only display trusted, vetted connection options. This code adds a malicious option not present in the official UI.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: UI overlays are used for legitimate wallet selection, but not for phishing or redirection.
key_indicators: Unexpected modal overlays with altered wallet options
UI elements not present in official releases

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises npm account of former Ledger employee via phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious package versions

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious versions (1.1.5, 1.1.6, 1.1.7) of Ledger Connect Kit to npm.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to dApps and users

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in user browsers when connecting wallets or signing transactions via dApps.
attack_chain.leads_to: User transactions are intercepted and redirected

attack_chain.action: User funds are silently drained to attacker-controlled wallet.
Ledger releases patched version (1.1.8) and notifies users.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attack stopped, but funds already stolen

behavioral_signatures: Runtime interception and modification of web3 transaction data
Injection of rogue wallet connection options or overlays
Silent redirection of transaction destination addresses
Discrepancy between npm package versions and Git tags/releases
file_indicators: dist/index.js containing 'MinimaDrainerValue' or similar obfuscated variables
Presence of unexpected modal overlays in dApp UI
npm package versions not present in official Git repository
network_indicators: Transactions sent to known attacker wallet addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm package versions that lack corresponding Git tags/releases, scan for obfuscated or minified code containing suspicious variables (e.g., 'MinimaDrainerValue'), and detect runtime modification of transaction data or injection of rogue wallet connection options. Monitor network traffic for connections to untrusted WalletConnect endpoints and for transactions being redirected to known attacker wallet addresses.
